study.title: A new song for all the earth
study.intro: Psalm 96 calls the whole world to sing a new song to the LORD. It urges God's people to tell the nations of His glory, exposes idols as nothing, invites every family of the earth to worship, and ends with all creation rejoicing because the LORD is coming to judge the world in righteousness.
study.context: Psalm 96 is one of the 'LORD reigns' psalms of Book IV. Nearly all of it also appears in 1 Chronicles 16:23-33, part of the song of thanks sung when David brought the ark to Jerusalem. Verses 1-3 call for singing and mission; verses 4-6 explain God's greatness over idols; verses 7-10 summon the nations to worship; verses 11-13 call creation to rejoice at His coming. Its vision looks ahead to the gospel going to all peoples.
study.peopleNote: David is linked because 1 Chronicles 16 records a version of this psalm sung when he brought the ark to Jerusalem. Jesus is linked as the coming King and Judge whose good news goes to all nations. God is never portrayed as a human body in planned art.

verses.title: A new song
verses.heading: All the earth sings
verses.meaning: The psalm opens, 'Sing to the LORD a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth.' A new song answers fresh acts of God's mercy. It is not just new music but renewed wonder. And the call is global: not only Israel but all the earth is invited. From the start, this psalm looks beyond one nation to a world united in praising the true God.
verses.context: 1 Chronicles 16:23 begins the parallel: 'Sing to the LORD, all the earth.' Isaiah 42:10 says, 'Sing to the LORD a new song—His praise from the ends of the earth.' Revelation 5:9 records a new song praising the Lamb who redeemed people from every nation.
explore: New song
A fresh song of praise responding to new mercies and God's saving acts.
All the earth
Every nation and people, showing God's worship is meant to be worldwide.
verses.reflect: What fresh mercy from God could inspire a 'new song' from you this week?
verses.alt: People of many lands gather singing on a broad grassy hillside.

verses.title: Day after day
verses.heading: Proclaim His salvation
verses.meaning: Verse 2 continues: 'Sing to the LORD, bless His name; proclaim His salvation day after day.' Praise is not a once-a-year event. Every day brings a reason to speak of God's rescue. 'Proclaim' means to announce good news, the same idea behind the word 'gospel.' The worshiper becomes a messenger, telling what God has done again and again.
verses.context: Isaiah 52:7 praises the feet of those who bring good news and proclaim salvation. Psalm 71:15 says, 'My mouth will declare Your righteousness and Your salvation all day long.' Acts 5:42 says the apostles never stopped proclaiming Jesus day after day.
explore: Bless His name
To praise and honor God's character and reputation with grateful words.
Proclaim
To announce publicly, like a herald spreading good news.
verses.reflect: How could you mention God's goodness naturally in an ordinary conversation today?
verses.alt: A messenger runs along a mountain road at dawn carrying news.

verses.title: Among the nations
verses.heading: Declare His glory
verses.meaning: Verse 3 widens the mission: 'Declare His glory among the nations, His wonders among all peoples.' God's people are not meant to keep His glory to themselves. Every nation deserves to hear what He has done. This verse anticipates Jesus' command to make disciples of all nations. Missions grow from worship: those who have seen God's wonders want everyone to know Him.
verses.context: Genesis 12:3 promises all families of the earth will be blessed through Abraham. Matthew 28:19 records Jesus saying, 'Go and make disciples of all nations.' Habakkuk 2:14 says the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the LORD's glory.
explore: Glory
The weight and splendor of God's greatness revealed for others to see.
Wonders
Amazing acts of God that cause awe, such as miracles and rescues.
verses.reflect: Who in your life has not yet heard of God's wonders, and how might you share them?
verses.alt: Travelers from different lands listen around a fire at a crossroads.

verses.title: Greatly to be praised
verses.heading: Feared above all gods
verses.meaning: Verse 4 explains why: 'For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; He is to be feared above all gods.' His greatness calls for matching praise. Small praise for a great God does not fit. To 'fear' Him means deep reverence and awe. The nations feared their idols, but the LORD alone deserves that reverence, because He alone is truly great and powerful.
verses.context: Psalm 48:1 says, 'Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised.' Deuteronomy 10:17 calls Him 'God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, mighty, and awesome God.' Revelation 15:4 asks, 'Who will not fear You, O Lord?'
explore: Greatly praised
Honored with praise that matches the immense greatness of God.
Fear
Reverent awe and respect toward God, recognizing His holiness and power.
verses.reflect: Does your praise of God match His greatness, or is it often small and hurried?
verses.alt: A vast starry sky arches above a small village on a hill.

verses.title: Idols and the heavens
verses.heading: Who made the skies
verses.meaning: Verse 5 makes a sharp contrast: 'For all the gods of the nations are idols, but it is the LORD who made the heavens.' The Hebrew word for idols sounds like 'nothings' or 'worthless things.' Statues of wood and stone made by human hands cannot do anything. The LORD, by contrast, made the very heavens. The real God creates; false gods are created.
verses.context: Isaiah 44:9 says those who fashion idols are nothing and their treasures are worthless. Jeremiah 10:11-12 contrasts gods that did not make the heavens with God who made the earth by His power. Acts 14:15 urges turning from worthless things to the living God.
explore: Idols
Images or objects worshiped as gods, which Scripture calls empty and powerless.
Heavens
The skies and everything above, including sun, moon and stars, made by God.
verses.reflect: What modern 'idols' promise much but cannot actually help you?
verses.alt: Broken clay figurines lie in the dust beneath a bright blue sky.

verses.title: Strength and beauty
verses.heading: His sanctuary filled
verses.meaning: Verse 6 describes God's presence: 'Splendor and majesty are before Him; strength and beauty fill His sanctuary.' These qualities are pictured like royal attendants standing before a king. God's dwelling is not dull or empty; it overflows with strength and loveliness. Worship brings us into the presence of beauty itself. True power and true beauty meet perfectly in God.
verses.context: Psalm 27:4 longs 'to gaze on the beauty of the LORD.' 1 Chronicles 16:27 says, 'Strength and joy fill His dwelling.' Isaiah 33:17 says, 'Your eyes will see the King in His beauty.'
explore: Splendor
Brilliant, glorious brightness that displays greatness.
Sanctuary
A holy place set apart for God's presence and the worship of His people.
verses.reflect: Where have you glimpsed God's beauty recently, in creation, people or worship?
verses.alt: Sunlight streams into a stone courtyard decorated with carved pomegranates.

verses.title: Families of the nations
verses.heading: Ascribe glory and strength
verses.meaning: Verse 7 calls out: 'Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the nations, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.' To ascribe means to give credit where it is due. Every family on earth is invited to recognize God's glory. The repeated 'ascribe' builds like a drumbeat. Worship is not giving God something He lacks; it is acknowledging what is already true about Him.
verses.context: Psalm 29:1 calls heavenly beings to 'ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.' Revelation 7:9 pictures a multitude from every nation worshiping before the throne. Ephesians 3:15 says every family in heaven and on earth derives its name from the Father.
explore: Ascribe
To credit or attribute something to someone, here acknowledging God's qualities.
Families of the nations
All the clans and peoples of the earth, invited to worship together.
verses.reflect: How might your family acknowledge God's glory together this week?
verses.alt: Several families from different lands stand together on a wide plain.

verses.title: Bring an offering
verses.heading: Enter His courts
verses.meaning: Verse 8 goes further: 'Ascribe to the LORD the glory due His name; bring an offering and enter His courts.' Worship involves both words and gifts. Bringing an offering showed gratitude and dependence. Remarkably, the nations are invited into the temple courts, not kept out. God's house is meant to be 'a house of prayer for all nations.' Generosity and worship go together.
verses.context: Isaiah 56:7 says, 'My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations.' Mark 11:17 records Jesus quoting this when cleansing the temple. Romans 12:1 urges offering our bodies as living sacrifices.
explore: Offering
A gift brought to God as an act of worship, thanks or devotion.
Courts
The open courtyards of the temple where worshipers gathered.
verses.reflect: What offering of time, money or service could you bring to God this week?
verses.alt: Worshipers carry baskets of grain through a stone gateway.

verses.title: Splendor of holiness
verses.heading: Tremble before Him
verses.meaning: Verse 9 says, 'Worship the LORD in the splendor of His holiness; tremble before Him, all the earth.' Holiness is God's perfect purity and otherness, and it is beautiful. Worship involves wonder and trembling together. God is not casual or ordinary. Joy and awe are not opposites but partners. The right response to His holiness is both delight and a humble, reverent trembling.
verses.context: Isaiah 6:3 records seraphim calling, 'Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts.' Hebrews 12:28 urges worship with reverence and awe. Psalm 2:11 says, 'Serve the LORD with fear and rejoice with trembling.'
explore: Holiness
God's absolute purity and set-apartness from all sin and limitation.
Tremble
To shake with awe before overwhelming greatness and holiness.
verses.reflect: How can you bring both joy and reverence to your worship of God?
verses.alt: Morning light floods a hushed temple courtyard as people bow.

verses.title: Declare: The LORD reigns
verses.heading: Judging with equity
verses.meaning: Verse 10 is the message for the nations: 'Declare among the nations: The LORD reigns! The world is firmly established; it cannot be moved; He will judge the peoples with equity.' This is good news. God's rule brings stability and fairness. Unlike corrupt human rulers, He judges with perfect equity, showing no favoritism. His reign is the world's hope.
verses.context: Psalm 93:1 also declares, 'The LORD reigns!' Acts 10:34 says God shows no favoritism. Isaiah 11:4 says the coming King will judge the poor with righteousness and decide with equity.
explore: Reigns
Rules as king with full authority over all peoples and creation.
Equity
Fairness and evenhandedness, treating all people justly without favoritism.
verses.reflect: Why is God's fair rule good news for people who suffer injustice?
verses.alt: A herald stands at a city gate announcing to a gathered crowd.

verses.title: Heavens glad, sea resounding
verses.heading: Creation rejoices
verses.meaning: Verse 11 calls all creation to celebrate: 'Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice; let the sea resound, and all that fills it.' The sky, the land and the ocean join the song. Creation itself longs for God's just rule. The roaring sea, once a picture of chaos, now thunders in praise. Everything God made is meant to rejoice in His reign.
verses.context: Psalm 98:7 says, 'Let the sea resound, and all that fills it.' Romans 8:21 says creation will be set free from bondage to decay. Revelation 5:13 pictures every creature in heaven, earth and sea praising God.
explore: Resound
To echo loudly, like the roar of waves becoming a song of praise.
Rejoice
To be filled with gladness and to express that joy openly in praise and song.
verses.reflect: Where in nature do you sense creation praising God?
verses.alt: Waves crash joyfully under a bright sky full of seabirds.

verses.title: Fields and forests
verses.heading: Trees sing for joy
verses.meaning: Verse 12 continues: 'Let the fields exult, and all that is in them. Then all the trees of the forest will sing for joy.' The picture is playful and vivid. Fields of grain sway and forests rustle as if dancing and singing. When God's rule is fully established, the whole created world will be set right. Even trees anticipate the joy of His coming.
verses.context: Isaiah 55:12 says, 'All the trees of the field will clap their hands.' 1 Chronicles 16:33 has the same line about trees singing. Luke 19:40 records Jesus saying that if people kept silent, the stones would cry out.
explore: Exult
To rejoice greatly, with the triumph and celebration of a victory festival.
Forest
A large area of trees, here pictured singing in praise to God.
verses.reflect: How can noticing creation's beauty stir you to praise God today?
verses.alt: Golden wheat fields sway beside a forest in a warm breeze.

verses.title: He is coming
verses.heading: Judging in righteousness
verses.meaning: The psalm ends with verse 13: creation sings 'before the LORD, for He is coming, He is coming to judge the earth. He will judge the world in righteousness and the peoples in His faithfulness.' The doubled 'He is coming' rings with excitement. God's judgment is not something to dread for those who trust Him; it means wrongs set right. Christians see this fulfilled when Jesus returns.
verses.context: Acts 17:31 says God has set a day when He will judge the world in righteousness by the Man He appointed. Revelation 22:20 records Jesus saying, 'Yes, I am coming soon.' 2 Peter 3:13 looks for a new earth where righteousness dwells.
explore: Righteousness
Perfect rightness and justice according to God's holy standard.
Faithfulness
God's reliability in keeping every promise, here in how He judges.
verses.reflect: How does the promise of God's coming shape the way you live today?
verses.alt: A bright dawn breaks over a peaceful valley with a long road.
